text: A king came home from Egypt and ordered a pyramid built in his kingdom. His court laughed, a pyramid in a land of rain. His people called it the king's sand castle. Every farmer gave a month a year to drag stones, but stone costs gold. Across the river, his rival laughed and built walls, markets, and a harbor instead. 20 years later, it was finished and nothing happened. His treasury was empty and his people threw mud at it. His rival sent him a gift, a little pyramid of sand. Then, one spring, the rain didn't stop for nine days. The old king rang every bell and ordered everyone up the steps. Half the town laughed. Suddenly, the river broke its banks. It swallowed the fields, the houses, and the rivals harbor. By morning, only the pyramids stood above the water, packed with people, goats, and cows. You see, in Egypt, he had watched the river flood the land. The houses went under, the pyramids never did. At home, he had found an old flood mark above the roofs. Their river did that once in a lifetime and it had been 70 years. Walls fall, but water can't push over a mountain of stone. They laughed at the king's tomb until it was the only thing that didn't drown.
